newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan doctors' strike drags on.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan doctors' strike drags on.

text.p: Legal proceedings were started on Tuesday against striking public doctors whose work stoppage, officials said, has already caused 15 deaths because of apparent lack of adequate medical care.
"Doctors found responsible in each individual case that is being investigated will be sanctioned, this is not open to negotiations," National Public Prosecutor Ivan Dario Badell said.

With a health system on the brink of collapse after 12 days of strikes by the country's 25,000 doctors, President Rafael Caldera faced one of the worst crises in the public sector since he took office nearly three years ago.

Doctors, who have even stopped work in emergency wards to demand a big pay increase, voted on Monday whether to continue the strike. They rejected the government's verbal offer of a 25 percent raise in line with other public sector employees.
They want their monthly take-home pay, including bonuses, to be increased from an average of $304 to $1,000.

Government officials said declaring a national health emergency, once contemplated, was not on the agenda. It would mean a militarization of all 380 hospitals and 4,000 ambulance services, but Defence Minister Pedro Nicola Valencia said: "This is not being planned so far, the military are only reinforcing emergency services."

He told reporters about 60 percent of the country's 2,500 military doctors were working at emergency and intensive care wards, mostly in the capital Caracas and in the western state of Zulia, where a cholera outbreak has killed 11 with nearly 300 cases reported over the past month.
